summary: Refine the already-implemented Bare Hands V1 UI: first-class HUD lifecycle control, right-click quick actions, fixed left tool palette, visual help, settings cleanup, full-screen calibration/tutorial experience, and real window move/resize practice.
locked_constraints: Do not redefine existing contextual Bare Hands interaction semantics; inherit docs/barehands-contracts.md and the prior jarvis-bare-hands-v1 task.
Bare Hands main HUD button uses a hand icon and mirrors OFF/SLEEP/ACTIVE from the real controller state.
OFF is dim grey, SLEEP uses normal Jarvis blue, ACTIVE uses brighter electric blue with a subtle glow; ACTIVE is not green.
Normal click opens a visual three-state chooser, not a text dropdown; right click opens Settings, Calibration, Help/Gestures, Diagnostics.
Expose only existing tools pointer, pan and select in a fixed vertical left palette; do not add new tools.
Remove lifecycle/tool/tutorial usage controls from the primary Settings information architecture.
Remove the separate user-facing Tutorial flow; calibration becomes the guided learning flow.
Calibration uses a full-screen blurred overlay without a centered modal and reserves the center for the exercise.
Calibration steps have a minimum reading phase and do not start measurement timeouts until the user can actually engage the exercise.
Calibration steps are resting hand, C wake pose, primary pinch, secondary pinch, target pinch, window move+resize sub-steps, completion.
The virtual hand is simple schematic/robotic line art, not realistic.
Window practice must use the real Bare Hands frame target/capture/geometry semantics rather than a fake drag widget.
planning_blockers: Workspace Task Type vocabulary is not exposed here; Slice 00 must assign valid existing Task Types before implementation dispatch.
Slice 00 must decide the safest backward-compatible migration for the existing tutorial voice/MCP command, but no separate tutorial UI/flow may remain.
